logic_errors.title: Explicit requests with a registered scope bypass authoritative branch continuity
logic_errors.finding: Scope resolution, inflight checks, replay history and pin tracking run only when automatic is true. An explicit alias request carrying valid generation/branch/invocation headers is recorded with scope=-1. Its observed tool response cannot pin the registered branch, cannot advance last_row, and does not invalidate old automatic advice. Subsequent auto requests can omit that exchange and reuse the previous replayable history and snapshot.
logic_errors.reproduction: Obtain format_simple advice after auto turn 1; send explicit baseline turn 2 with the same scope and a distinct invocation; scripted backend returns a tool_calls response. Submit auto turn 3 using turn-1 history plus a new user message and omit the tool exchange. Both normal and ASan builds dispatch turn 3 to cheaper physical instead of retaining frontier/blocking.
logic_errors.expected: All associated physical requests must update/invalidate authoritative branch state regardless of whether selection is explicit. Preserve explicit alias semantics without allowing explicit requests to bypass inflight exclusion, scope validation or continuity evidence. A conservative rejection/pin on mixing modes is acceptable.

logic_errors.title: Shadow selector veto changes actual request acceptance
logic_errors.finding: rc_select failure returns 403 before the g->active check. Shadow is therefore not proposal-only: candidate-registry context limits can block the baseline dispatch even though M2 permits it and no interpretation exists.
logic_errors.reproduction: Configure mode=shadow and baseline candidate context_limit=1. A plain auto request without association dispatches baseline and returns 200; the identical body with freshly registered scope headers is 403 with no upstream dispatch. Reproduced in normal and ASan builds.
logic_errors.expected: In shadow, record an invalid/blocked proposal without applying the optional selector veto to actual dispatch. Keep mandatory final M2 and real authoritative continuity enforcement.

suggestions.note: Shadow also changes a clean subsequent request from frontier to physical after sensitive source evidence. This is conservative, not an exposure, but contradicts an unqualified proposal-only shadow claim. Reconcile/document the M2-derived authority exception rather than weakening privacy enforcement.
GET /v1/models lists configured explicit aliases but omits the configured auto_alias; clarify discovery expectations or add coverage.

Qualification is operator-configured task bits plus a nonempty evidence label; economics are static expected_task_cost quotes, not measured cache residency/replay/interpreter accounting. Current user-message semantics are not independently validated against an old format_simple prediction. Do not present these fixtures as validated quality or cheapest-total-task proof.

summary: Do not land this frozen snapshot unchanged: existing normal and sanitizer suites pass, but independent HTTP probes reproduce a continuity bypass through scoped explicit aliases and an active shadow-selector veto. This is not full M3 acceptance.

verification.environment: Existing recursant-v4-dev:local image 2b5edaf312e5; docker --pull never --network none --user 1000:1000; snapshot mounted /src:ro; independent writable build mounts; no published ports.

independent_probes.note: Script captures adversarial observations rather than asserting the currently incorrect results are correct; verdict above evaluates them.

client_cancellation.probe: TCP RST while scoped upstream is delayed; next request after teardown succeeds on original frontier owner, not a stranded inflight 409

verification.positive_review: Separate source/inference bearers and fixed server-owned tenant/project; strict source/config schemas; boot-scoped generation; duplicate invocation/header ambiguity and loss fail closed; accepted revision/sequence replay fencing; rejected newer-source advice revocation; private-only interpreter; concrete candidate M2 rechecks plus final M2; delayed interpretation does not block dispatch; disabled/no-context regression tests pass.
verification.compatibility: Read base 9cb10db runtime.c/router.c via git show. Unknown runtime keys were already rejected at baseline; their continued rejection is not a new regression. Existing router/compliance passthrough regression suites pass. Baseline binary was not separately rebuilt.

limitations: Review applies only to these frozen file hashes, not an author final commit or subsequent changes.
No real inference, model installation, public networking, Hermes profile changes, service changes or source-code modifications.

All integration/backend/interpreter replies are scripted loopback HTTP. This proves actual C listener/transport behavior, not native Hermes closed-loop causality, semantic accuracy, held-out qualification, cache economics, dollar savings or full M3.
Acknowledged worker OOM serialization issue M3-INTERPRETER-002 is excluded as a separate fix in progress; sanitizer success here is not allocation-fault injection coverage.
Single configured principal only, not multi-tenant isolation certification. No fuzzing, sustained production load, complete allocation-failure campaign or exhaustive cancellation timing proof.
